description: Cross-language conformance test vectors for canonical serialization v1.0 (Record §3), under the hashed field set as revised in 0.8.0 (Record §4.1). Each envelope-v1.0 input holds exactly the eleven hashed names, so the whole input and its hashed fields serialize to the same bytes. Entries under `negativeVectors` MUST raise in every SDK; a canonicalizer that returns bytes for any of them is broken.

vectors.description: Numeric edge cases — zero, negative, small decimal
Unicode supplementary characters (emoji) in keys and values — verifies Unicode code point sort order
vectors.note: JavaScript's default .sort() uses UTF-16 code unit comparison. For supplementary characters (emoji), this produces the same order as Unicode code point order within the BMP and supplementary planes separately. Keys sort as: 'a' (U+0061), '📊' (U+1F4CA), '🔒' (U+1F512) — ASCII before supplementary, then supplementary by code point.

vectors.description: ModelDescriptor canonical bytes — populated set-valued fields, supplied unsorted (the set sub-rule sorts each one)
vectors.note: Input arrays are deliberately out of order: regulatoryMarkings by (authority,identifier) sorts (eu-ce-mdr,CE1) before (us-fda,K2); training.evaluations by name sorts arc-challenge before mmlu; externalIdentifiers by (scheme,value) sorts (doi,10.0/y) before (hf-repo,meta-llama/x).

vectors.description: Number rendering follows JS Number::toString — 1e-6/1e21 thresholds, unpadded exponent, >17-significant-digit integer-valued floats
vectors.note: Every literal is written with an exponent or a decimal point on purpose: without one it parses back as a Python int, and integers outside +/-(2^53-1) are refused rather than rendered differently in the two SDKs. Negative zero is covered by a unit test instead — JSON cannot carry it.

vectors.description: ModelDescriptor set-valued sub-rule sorts by UTF-16 code unit, not Unicode code point
vectors.note: U+1F600 is supplementary-plane: its first UTF-16 code unit is 0xD83D, BELOW U+FF21 (0xFF21). Python's default string sort compares code points and orders these the other way round, so this vector discriminates the two orders.

vectors.description: Object key order discriminates UTF-16 code-unit sort from Unicode code-point sort
vectors.note: V16's three keys sort identically under both orderings, which its own note admits, so it cannot catch a sort regression. This one can: U+FF01 is a BMP key whose single code unit is 0xFF01; U+1F600 is astral and its FIRST code unit is 0xD83D. UTF-16 order puts the emoji first; code-point order puts U+FF01 first. Any switch to code-point key ordering in either SDK changes these bytes.
